control: IDENTITY (control 2) and its POSITIVE control, measured on pixels
member: july31/set-03 group 1, the three arms' sub-stacks
instrument: astropy.io.fits read + numpy difference — an INDEPENDENT reader, deliberately not Siril: a tool's own statistic cannot check whether that tool's operation damaged an image. Diagnostic only; reads no deliverable and gates nothing.

IDENTITY_A_vs_I.what: the per-set flat run a second time through arm B's slot
IDENTITY_A_vs_I.verdict: TRUE ZERO at every group and at the composed level — the arm-B
machinery introduces nothing, and the compose registration is
pinned across arms as well as the per-group registration

POSITIVE_CONTROL_A_vs_B.what: the SAME comparison, same code path, on the one-knob pair
POSITIVE_CONTROL_A_vs_B.verdict: DIFFERS everywhere — so the zeros above are RESULTS, not a check
POSITIVE_CONTROL_A_vs_B.note_worth_carrying: the composed max|diff| 0.00766 is a THIRD of g1's
member-level 0.0228, which is the compose-level cancellation
showing up in the crudest possible statistic

why_both_lines_belong_together: An identity control returning 0 differing pixels is the exact shape this repo's most persistent defect takes: a check that cannot fail (the `Found [0-9]+ star` regex that never matched, so a validation gate read 0 unconditionally). The registry requires the falsification be EXECUTED, not argued. The A-vs-B pair supplies it on the same code path and fires at 99.9998% of pixels, so the identity zero is discriminating rather than vacuous. Raised by a peer session's audit; re-measured here rather than accepted.

the_whole-file_cmp_is_the_WRONG_test_and.what_happened: `cmp -s` on the two products reports NOT byte-identical while the pixels are bit-identical.
the_whole-file_cmp_is_the_WRONG_test_and.cause: Siril stamps its own creation DATE on every product and the chain stamps PIPEREV (the repo revision). Those two keys are the ONLY header differences; HISTORY is identical at 3 entries and no key is present in one file and absent in the other.
the_whole-file_cmp_is_the_WRONG_test_and.why_this_is_more_than_a_tidy_up: a check that fires spuriously trains the operator to bypass it, which is how a real failure gets waved through later. The byte test is replaced by a pixel test rather than silently ignored.
the_whole-file_cmp_is_the_WRONG_test_and.bonus_result_from_the_variance_that_did_: arm A g1 was built at PIPEREV ed9b026 and arm I g1 at 906381c, so the records-only commits made between them are MEASURED PIXEL-NEUTRAL for this route (0 differing pixels across both). Commits are held for the remaining arms so PIPEREV stays uniform.

md5_values_are_CONVENTION_DEPENDENT_and_.resolution: FITS data is big-endian, so a hash taken on the array AS READ differs from one taken after a native-order cast — the same pixels, two digests. Two sessions reported different digests for the same file and both were right. Quote a pixel-difference COUNT, which is convention-free; a bare md5 is only comparable within one convention, so the convention is recorded beside every digest here.
md5_values_are_CONVENTION_DEPENDENT_and_.what_both_sessions_agreed_on_independent: A vs I = 0 differing pixels, max|diff| exactly 0.

one_knob_verified_by_HEADER_not_asserted.REGPIN: armreg_g1.seq — registration data pinned across arms, so the homographies and the reference index are the donor's

CALXSET.note: the builder stamps CALXSET when --flat is not the flat the set's record names. Here that is a cross-WINDOW calibration within one set, not the cross-SET reuse README step 1b bans; the key conflates the two. Correct as a flag that the product was not built with the recorded flat, imprecise as a name.
